safety_verdicts.content: Patient presents with lip swelling for the past 1 hour.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts mention lip swelling but do not document the duration of ~1 hour.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the ~1 hour duration of lip swelling reduces the precision of the acute timeline, which can be relevant for assessing progression and urgency in suspected allergic reactions. However, the encounter already identifies escalating symptoms and directs emergency care, so the incremental harm is limited.

If dizziness was truly present, leaving it out could understate systemic involvement (e.g., evolving anaphylaxis/hypotension) and might affect monitoring intensity. In this case, more critical red-flag symptoms (breathing/throat concerns) are already captured and prompt emergency escalation, limiting added harm.
